newsitem.title: USA: Uni-Marts says sees Q4 loss $0.15 to $0.21.
newsitem.headline: Uni-Marts says sees Q4 loss $0.15 to $0.21.

text.p: Uni-Marts Inc said Friday it expects to report a loss for the 1997 second fiscal quarter ending April 3, 1997 of between $1 million and $1.4 million, or a loss of $0.15 and $0.21 per share, because of lower-than-expected results from new stores.
Uni-Marts reported earnings of $254,278, or $0.04 per share, for the previous year's second fiscal quarter ended April 4, 1996. "The anticipated loss is due to lower than
expected contributions from newly constructed and remodeled stores," said Uni-Marts Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Henry D. Sahakian.

"Over the past three fiscal years and first two quarters of the current fiscal year, we have invested approximately $40 million in new store construction and remodeling projects, including larger gasoline facilities and the installation of branded fast-food units.

"While we are incurring the full cost of the additional labor, depreciation and interest associated with these expenditures, merchandise revenue, gasoline gallon and merchandise margin increases continue to be well below our original expectations.

"We are taking steps designed to attain expected returns on these new investments. These include postponement of new store construction, remodeling and upgrading existing stores, and acquisitions," he said.
